reason: The Book of Esther is uniquely distinguished by the complete absence of any explicit reference to Yahweh/God throughout the entire narrative. There are no divine speeches, complaints, or pronouncements of any kind. The text is entirely focused on human characters and political events—the Persian court, Ahasuerus, Esther, Mordecai, and Haman—without any theological complaint framework. The narrative presents the deliverance of the Jewish people through human agency alone, not through divine complaint or intervention.
